critical_code_review_comments: _normalize_extensions signature is loosely typed (accepts anything) and silently returns None for unsupported input like dicts. This is safe because Pydantic AssignmentCreate/Update enforce Optional[List[str]] at the API boundary. Direct calls with list-of-dicts would stringify each dict and store the stringified form — not blocking, just noteworthy for future direct callers.

_effective_allowed_extensions correctly treats an empty list [] as 'no override' (line 892: `if override:` — empty list is falsy). This makes PUT with [] clear the override AND fall back to type default consistently on subsequent submissions — behavior matches the spec.

Error message in submit endpoints uses the EFFECTIVE list (override values shown when override exists), giving students accurate feedback — verified in test_override_rejects_txt_with_override_in_error.

Frontend AssignmentFormDialog handleSave (AssignmentsTab.js:311-315) mirrors backend normalization — parses comma/space/semicolon, strips leading dot, lowercases, filters empties. Empty input → null → backend stores null → next submit falls back to defaults. Round-trip complete.
